analysis:
Actual maintained Native direct player with authored10000-cue ordered plain external captions, identical bounded SRT-to-VTT preparation in all arms, and unchanged H264/stereoAAC ownership. Candidate retained at most11 VTTCues versus10000 in shipping Blob-loaded and cheaper JS-eager controls. Five forward/backward seeks matched authored active intervals/text and visible subtitle pixels exactly; independent wrong-source text changed9606 caption channels; overlap rejected with prior-owner preservation, source replacement/stale events, delayed-read cancellation, EOF and cleanup passed. Five alternating three-arm whole-player trials: versus baseline: median startup saving 1.407% (18.900ms), open-through-EOF CPU change 0.241%, peak summed RSS saving 1.559% (14720.0KiB); versus eager: median startup saving -0.178% (-2.351ms), open-through-EOF CPU change 1.359%, peak summed RSS saving -0.565% (-5216.0KiB). Primary startup and whole-session CPU tradeoff gates failed. Cue count is not a memory measurement; retained full caption source/parsed records remain charged.

Do not integrate this whole-player profile on the historical component saving alone. Reopen with a representative workload demonstrating meaningful startup or total-memory benefit against the cheapest correct eager owner without a meaningful session CPU regression.
